coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks
record.distance_note: Piers 68 & 70's dry-dock and ship-repair facility sits immediately north of Brookfield's tracked 28-acre Pier 70 redevelopment parcel and Crane Cove Park, outside both -- Port materials describe it as a separate 13-acre facility, closed in 2017, at the complex's northeast corner.

how_to_comment.detail: Agenda items on the Pier 68/70 dry docks

how_to_comment.channel: Clerk of the Board of Supervisors

record.summary: Two Port-owned floating dry docks at Piers 68 & 70 -- Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock -- that the Port Commission declared an emergency over on 2025-12-08 after hull tears and uncontrolled ballast-tank flooding caused Dry Dock No. 2 to list. The Port is stabilizing both structures and plans to demolish and dispose of them, at a total estimated cost of $61.2M, of which about $20.0M was secured as of February 2026.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- a coarse placeholder box, not a traced footprint. This is a Port tideland facility with no Assessor parcel and no source site plan or GIS shapefile was found to digitize the actual dry-dock basins, cranes and sheds from. The box is anchored to two real points (the 20th/Illinois St intersection, and the narrow real gap between Pier 70's and Mission Bay South's own tracked geometry) but does not represent the true shape or full extent of the 13-acre shipyard, which projects east into the Bay beyond what a land-based box can show. Needs replacement with a real digitized footprint if a Port GIS layer or the Dry Dock Memorandum's own site figure becomes available.
notes.digitized_from: No Assessor block/lot exists for this Port tideland/water-lot facility (confirmed: DataSF's 'Parcels - Active and Retired' Socrata dataset, acdm-wktn, has no PIER-numbered street_name entries at all near this site, consistent with pier and dry-dock structures sitting outside the Assessor's secured roll). No Port GIS shapefile or site-plan figure for the Piers 68/70 shipyard footprint was available to digitize from directly, so this is a coarse locational box only, centered near the shipyard's known entrance at 20th and Illinois St (real DataSF street-centerline intersection, data/raw/official_street_centerlines.geojson) and sized to sit between the tracked Pier 70 parcel's own northern edge (Crane Cove Park, data/manual/pier70_crane_cove_park.geojson, max latitude 37.76406) and Mission Bay South's nearest tracked features (the UCSF Illinois Street Garage and the P24 waterfront lawn, data/processed/approximate_projects.geojson, both of which reach south to roughly latitude 37.7644-37.7648) -- the real Piers 68/70 shipyard, described in Port materials as a 13-acre facility at the 'northeast corner' of the complex including Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock, occupies this narrow shoreline gap and extends east into the Bay itself, which this box does not attempt to trace.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Port tideland/water-lot facility; not on the Assessor's secured roll (data.sf.gov acdm-wktn has no PIER-numbered parcels near this site).
notes.regulatory_context: Dry Dock No. 2 (a ~1940s-era floating dry dock) developed excessive listing after hull tears and uncontrolled ballast-tank flooding in November 2025; the Port Commission President and Executive Director declared an emergency on 2025-12-08 (Port Commission memo, Calendar Item 9A, 2026-01-09). Port staff anticipate advertising a demolition-services contract in summer 2026 for Dry Dock No. 2 and the neighboring Eureka Dry Dock (a second floating dry dock at Piers 68/70, formerly USS Steadfast/AFDM-14 -- not the 1890 ferryboat Eureka at Hyde Street Pier/SF Maritime NHP). Total estimated cost of stabilization and disposal is $61.2M (Capital Planning Committee memo, 2026-02-09); see the record file for the funding breakdown and what remains unfunded.

facts.value: Two floating dry docks: Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock (the latter formerly USS Steadfast, AFDM-14 -- not the 1890 ferryboat Eureka preserved at Hyde Street Pier/SF Maritime NHP)

changes.text: New adjacent record for the Piers 68 & 70 dry docks (Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock), following the Port's December 2025 emergency declaration over Dry Dock No. 2's hull tears and listing, the January and February 2026 Port/Capital Planning Committee memos on stabilization and planned demolition, and Mission Local's February 2026 reporting on the $61.2M disposal cost.

open_questions: Whether the $18.5M Port Commission Resolution 24-51 authorization (Oct 2024) is a subset of, or additional to, the $61.2M total cost figure presented in the Feb 2026 Capital Planning Committee memo is not established by the sources reviewed here.

Whether demolition will be completed "before winter storms" (a claim in an owner-supplied unsourced summary, not repeated in this record) is not supported by any primary source found; SFist (2026-03-05) reports it will likely be a year before the dry dock situation is resolved, and roughly $41.2M of the $61.2M total remained unfunded as of Feb 2026.
What becomes of BAE Systems' ship-repair operations at the adjacent Pier 70 shipyard once these dry docks are removed is not addressed in the sources reviewed here.
